column1: # THE GAP IN AGNES'S OWN WINDOW, FOUND BY COUNTING THE SWEEPS INSTEAD OF TRUSTING THEM.
# Landesarchiv Berlin LABSA, Standesamt Spandau (Spandau I), P Rep. 480 Nr. 1238, 1239 and 1240.
# Work list rows 253 and 254. Read 11 October 2026.
# WHY. Row 253 looks for AGNES LEIBHOLZ née KERGER of Mehringdamm 109, who is in the Berlin
# telephone book to 1979-80 and gone from 1980-81. This archive has said since 8 October that all
# twelve West Berlin boroughs were swept. THEY WERE — BUT NOT ALL FROM THE SAME YEAR, and nobody
# had laid the twelve coverages side by side.

column2: value

column1: # ---------------- THE COVERAGE MATRIX, WHICH NOBODY HAD BUILT ----------------
what the twelve boroughs actually cover
column2: SCHÖNEBERG 1938-1994, all 61 volumes, closed 21 September · KREUZBERG 1938-1994, closed 11 October · REINICKENDORF 1974-1994 · NEUKÖLLN 1967-1992, which is the whole of LABSA's holding · CHARLOTTENBURG, STEGLITZ, TEMPELHOF, TIERGARTEN, WEDDING, WILMERSDORF and ZEHLENDORF 1967-1994, twenty-eight volumes each · *** AND SPANDAU I 1983-1994 ONLY. ***

column1: *** SO THERE WAS ONE GAP AND IT SAT EXACTLY WHERE SHE DISAPPEARS ***
column2: P Rep. 480 Nr. 1238 (1980), Nr. 1239 (1981) and Nr. 1240 (1240 is 1982) had never been swept. She leaves the telephone book between the 1979-80 and 1980-81 volumes. THE THREE UNREAD YEARS WERE HER THREE YEARS. That is not a near miss; it is the shape of a sweep that counted boroughs and not years.

column1: # ---------------- AND THE ONE VOLUME 7 OCTOBER LEFT OPEN IS NOW CLOSED, BY STRUCTURE ----------------
*** P REP. 480 NR. 2458 IS NOT A NAME INDEX AT ALL, WHATEVER THE CATALOGUE CALLS IT ***
column2: the 7 October sweep recorded it as "the one volume of the fifty-one that is neither read nor closed" — 202 pages, control 0.03, blind, and its relationship to the single-year volumes unestablished. Re-scored here at 0.030, the same figure, and then READ AT THE IMAGE. It is titled "Namensverzeichnis zum Sterberegister" AND IT IS A CHRONOLOGICAL RUNNING LIST: two columns a page of REGISTER NUMBER · FORENAME SURNAME, numbers ascending in register order, with date headings breaking the run — "3.5.1983" then 2073, 2074, 2075, and so on.

column1: which closes it without reading 202 faint pages
column2: it lists, in date order, the same deaths the single-year volumes index by name. SPANDAU I HAS A SINGLE-YEAR VOLUME FOR EVERY ONE OF 1982, 1983, 1984, 1985 AND 1986 — Nr. 1240, 1248, 2332, 2356 and 2459 — and 1983 to 1986 were read on 7 October and 1982 is read here. THE DUPLICATE ADDS NOTHING AND ITS SILENCE NEVER MATTERED. The catalogue description is wrong and that is worth more than the volume was.

column1: # ---------------- THE THREE VOLUMES, SCORED BEFORE THEY WERE BELIEVED ----------------
ALL THREE ARE LEGIBLE, SO THESE ARE REAL NEGATIVES
column2: Nr. 1238 (1980) 230 pages, 1.861 control names a page · Nr. 1239 (1981) 211 pages, 1.725 · Nr. 1240 (1982) 207 pages, 1.691. Against the archive's blind threshold of 0.15 and against the 0.030 of Nr. 2458 on the same shelf. These are typed indexes and the text layer reads them.

column1: *** NO KERGER. NOT ONCE, IN ANY OF THE THREE VOLUMES. ***
column2: and no LEIBHOLZ in 1980 or 1981. The only Leibholz in the three years is the 1982 entry already held, below.

column1: AND THE FORENAME IS ITS OWN CONTROL
column2: AGNES appears NINETY times in the 1980 volume, SEVENTY in 1981 and SEVENTY-EIGHT in 1982 — two hundred and thirty-eight other women. The instrument plainly reads that word on these pages. It is the surname that is absent, not the ability to see it.

column1: *** WHICH CLOSES THE QUESTION THE WAY A NEGATIVE SHOULD BE CLOSED ***
column2: AGNES LEIBHOLZ née KERGER DOES NOT APPEAR IN ANY WEST BERLIN DEATH REGISTER INDEX THAT EXISTS FOR HER WINDOW. Twelve boroughs, every year each one holds from 1967 or earlier to 1994 — and the last gap is now filled. She was 91 in 1980 and the index closes at 1994, when she would have been 105.

column1: what is left of her, and it is three readings
column2: SHE DIED OUTSIDE BERLIN — a move to family or to a home beyond the city, which is what her husband's own case warns about: Heinrich left the directory in 1942 and died in 1948, in a borough he did not live in. OR SHE DIED AFTER 1994 and the thirty-year closure still hides it. OR EAST BERLIN, which is the weakest of the three and now has a date under it rather than an intuition.

column1: and the East Berlin reasoning, measured rather than assumed
column2: LABSA holds ELEVEN East Berlin offices, 605 volumes, 41.9 GB — Mitte, Prenzlauer Berg, Friedrichshain, Treptow, Köpenick, Lichtenberg, Weißensee, Pankow, Marzahn, Hohenschönhausen, Hellersdorf. The 8 October sweep left them on the argument that "a West Berliner listed in a 1979 telephone book did not move to the DDR". THAT ARGUMENT IS RIGHT AND NOW HAS A BOUNDARY ON IT: until November 1989 a West Berlin pensioner could not relocate east at all, so East Berlin is only live for 1990-1994, when she would have been 101 to 105. Not swept, and the reason is a date and not a shrug.

column1: # ---------------- AND THE SWEEP TURNED UP A PERSON OF THE EIGHTH SPELLING ----------------
*** HERFERT verh. LEIPHOLZ · ELSE HEDWIG · 24.11. · 3483 · ev. · verh. ***
column2: Standesamt Spandau I, Sterberegister 1980 Nr. 3483, died 24 NOVEMBER 1980, evangelical, MARRIED. P Rep. 480 Nr. 1238 page 70, READ AT THE PAGE IMAGE — a typed index under the printed headings "Des Verstorbenen · Familienname · Vornamen · Todestag · Nr. des Sterbebuches · Zugehörigkeit zu einer Kirche". Filed between "Herfert, Anna Marie" and "Herfert geb. Postel, Klara Lina Rosa".

column1: what she is and what she is not
column2: BORN HERFERT, MARRIED A LEIPHOLZ. "verh." is verheiratet and the column says she was still married, so there was a living Mr Leipholz in Spandau in 1980. SET BESIDE WHAT THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD: ERNA LEIPHOLZ at Streitstraße 39, Spandau, in six consecutive telephone books from 1975-76 to 1980-81, on one number. TWO LEIPHOLZ PRESENCES IN ONE BOROUGH IN ONE WINDOW, and nothing joins them but that. NOT KIN TO ANYONE HERE ON ANY EVIDENCE — the eighth spelling is the directory's own cross-reference and it is not a pedigree.

column1: # ---------------- AND ROW 254'S WOMAN, CONFIRMED FROM A SECOND DIRECTION ----------------
the 1982 entry is independently re-found, and it is indexed TWICE
column2: Leibholz verh. Schönfeld · [forename withheld] · 19. 5. · 1486 · mos. · verw. on page 100, under L — AND "Schönfeld geb. Leibholz · [forename withheld] · 19. 5. · 1486 · mos. · verw." on page 168, under S. THE SAME REGISTER NUMBER FROM TWO UNRELATED POSITIONS IN THE SAME VOLUME, which is the pattern this archive first saw with Gerda Bade geb. Leibholz at Wilmersdorf in 1993.

column1: *** THE FORENAME STAYS WITHHELD AND THAT HAS NOT CHANGED ***
column2: row 254 withholds it because, set beside the surname she was born with, it is ALSO THE MAIDEN NAME OF A LIVING PERSON IN THIS FAMILY. It was read again here and it is not written down here. That is David's decision to reverse and not this archive's.

column1: # ---------------- A LIMIT ON FOUR READINGS MADE EARLIER TODAY ----------------
*** A WOMAN CAN BE INDEXED UNDER ONE NAME OR TWO, AND THESE VOLUMES DO BOTH ***
column2: the 1982 woman is cross-indexed under L and under S. ELSE HEDWIG IS NOT: she appears once, under H, and the word Leipholz is only the second element of her line. SO A READER WHO READS ONLY THE L BLOCK FINDS HER ONLY IF THE OFFICE HAPPENED TO CROSS-INDEX HER.

column1: *** AND IT DOES NOT WEAKEN THE SENTENCE ABOUT AGNES, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING BEFORE ANYONE ASKS ***
column2: the risk case is a woman whose NAME OF RECORD AT DEATH is not the family's — Else Hedwig died as a HERFERT, so the registrar had no reason to file her under L at all. AGNES'S NAME OF RECORD IS LEIBHOLZ AND THE TELEPHONE BOOK PROVES SHE USED IT: she is printed “Leibholz” at Mehringdamm 109 in every volume from 1972-73 to 1979-80. A widow who goes on being listed under her husband's surname for eight years is entered under it when she dies, as “Leibholz geb. Kerger”, WHICH IS AN L ENTRY. The twelve-borough sweeps also read WHOLE VOLUMES by text layer rather than L blocks, so both forms were in range there in any case; the limit bites only on the four Kreuzberg years that had to be read by band.

column1: and that bears on the Kreuzberg blind years read this morning
column2: KREUZBERG 1959, 1960, 1961 AND 1962 WERE READ BY L BLOCK AT THE IMAGE, because their text layers are blind and the whole volume could not be read. A woman born Kerger or Herfert or anything else who married into this surname, and whom that office did not cross-index, WOULD NOT BE IN THE BAND THAT WAS READ. The four negatives stand as what they are — no Leibholz, Leipholz or Leipsholz in the L block — and that is not the same sentence as "no woman of this family died in Kreuzberg in those years". IT IS RECORDED AS A LIMIT RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER AS A FAULT.

column1: near misses settled by eye, so nobody settles them twice
column2: LEIBNER verh. PODGURSKI and its mirror PODGURSKI geb. LEIBNER (1982, Nr. 2327) · LEIPNITZ, Kurt Erich (1982, Nr. 3492) · LEIPOLD · SLOWINSKI geb. METZLAFF (1981, Nr. 1701) · GINDLER geb. WILLUWEIT and WILLUWEIT verh. GINDLER (1982, Nr. 898) · SEJA geb. LUWE (1980, Nr. 3140).
